summary: @servicetitan/carto-charts-rn preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute a heavily obfuscated sibling payload
details: package.json declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime binary from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases (v1.3.13) at install time and then invokes it via execFileSync against a sibling file `math_init.js` (~727KB). math_init.js is heavily obfuscated using a shuffled numeric/string constant array with a rotation function (`WV8StW`) and mangled identifiers (`_0x...`); URL-like fragments are reconstructed at runtime rather than appearing as literals, hiding any network destinations from static inspection. setup.mjs itself is variable-mangled. The package advertises itself as a React Native chart wrapper under the ServiceTitan corporate npm scope but ships no native source (no C/C++/Rust, no binding.gyp) that would justify fetching a second JS runtime, and the obfuscated payload has no relationship to the stated charting purpose. Executing an obfuscated sibling script under a freshly-downloaded alternate runtime at preinstall is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern used to run attacker-controlled code on installer machines while evading Node-based static scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
